findings.ac: Status: failing log fetch keeps the PR red and big
findings.text: _failing_detail calls _gh('run','view',...,'--log-failed') unguarded; a GhError propagates out of gate_status to cmd_status, which emits verdict 'none' exit 0 (a false pass) instead of red+big. No test in test_ci_gate.py exercises a failing log fetch (FakeGh never raises).

findings.ac: Status: gh failure after the first read is pending
findings.text: gate_status has no try/except around the polling _gh('pr','view') calls; any GhError, including on the 2nd+ poll, is caught only in cmd_status and reported as verdict 'none' exit 0, not 'pending'. No test covers a mid-poll gh failure.

findings.ac: Status: missing gh is none (exit 0), unusable gh is cannot_run (exit 2)
findings.text: cmd_status maps every GhError (missing, unauthenticated, non-zero exit) to verdict 'none' exit 0; the status verdict set has no 'cannot_run' and no exit 2 path (only parity and cap use 2). test_status_gh_unavailable_is_none_exit_0 only covers the missing case; unusable gh is untested and unimplemented, so an unusable gh silently passes.

findings.ac: Fix path and wiring: exit 2 halts [CI-RED] could not check
findings.text: The string '[CI-RED] could not check' (or any exit-2/cannot_run handling for status) is absent from references/ci-gate.md, 4a step 7/8 and 3z Step 3A; the reference only defines [CI-PARITY] could not run. wiring tests never assert it.

findings.ac: Time-to-Value: one blocking call run with the host's maximum tool timeout
findings.text: Neither references/ci-gate.md, 4a step 8 nor 3z Step 3A tells the agent to run `ci_gate.py status` with the host's maximum tool timeout (script cap is 480 s, default tool timeouts are shorter), and no wiring test checks it; the 8-minute cap and no-checks skip are covered, the timeout instruction is not.

Issue Overview says the parity part was built, measured and dropped, and Notes say 'Not building ... a pre-push local CI replay', but ci_gate.py still ships cmd_parity/select_steps, references/ci-gate.md section 1, 4a step 4 and the [CI-PARITY] halts/parity:waived ship line, with wiring tests enforcing them. Code and docs contradict the final scope.

The gate fixture always patches _base_is_stale to False; no test asserts result['base_stale'] is True in status output (only classify(stale=True) is unit-tested), and _base_is_stale itself is untested.
